title: Aligning Large Language Model Agents with Rational and Moral Preferences: A Supervised Fine-Tuning Approach

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM action frequencies and beliefs in canonical economic games (Sequential Prisoner's Dilemma, Trust Game, Ultimatum Game) to measure excessive cooperation and insensitivity to monetary payoffs relative to human benchmarks and theoretical rational agents.

Testing LLM agents on the Moral Machine dilemma to measure self-other asymmetry and preference reversals between normative moral endorsements (utilitarian autonomous vehicles) and personal purchasing decisions when the passenger is oneself, a family member, or a coworker.

Simulating a repeated duopoly pricing game with logit demand to measure the tendency of LLM agents to engage in tacit algorithmic collusion by setting supra-competitive prices above the Nash equilibrium.
